clue.text: Liking the opposite sex in proper place

definitions.meaning: heterosexual, in the informal sense of the word
level and correctly positioned, as a picture hung true on a wall

explanation.definitionFit: The word means heterosexual informally and also means correctly aligned or tidy, as in putting a crooked frame right.

clue.text: Problem about elevating one who's fallen in social class

indicators.note: about means the word for a problem wraps around the rest

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevating means reading upward, so backwards

parts.note: a fallen woman, in old-fashioned terms a tart

explanation.surface: A problem arises over raising up someone who has slipped down the social ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one who's fallen' is the old-fashioned 'fallen woman'; 'elevating' reads her upward in this down clue before the problem goes about her.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratum is a level or layer in society, a social rank or class.

clue.text: In which people help themselves to Roy's fruit, showing no heart

parts.note: Rob Roy was the Scottish outlaw, so Roy's first name is Rob

indicators.note: showing no heart means the central letter of the fruit word is dropped

parts.note: berries are small fruits

explanation.surface: Thieves raid someone called Roy's fruit stall heartlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: Rob Roy MacGregor was an 18th-century Scottish outlaw. 'showing no heart' removes the middle R of BERRIES, giving BERIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Thefts are events where people help themselves to what is not theirs, a euphemism for stealing.

clue.text: Fly, perhaps, keeping pressure in check

indicators.note: keeping means the bug holds the pressure letter inside it

parts.note: a fly is an example of an insect
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: A fly is kept under pressure and held in check.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to examine or look it over carefully.

clue.text: Unpleasant feeling, leaving grand house

indicators.note: leaving means the letter for grand departs from the longer word

parts.note: the sick aftermath of drinking
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Someone feels rough and leaves a grand mansion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' means a royal dynasty, the House of Hanover, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal houses are dynasties, and this German line ruled Britain from George I to Victoria.

clue.text: Assortment in paperboy's satchel?

definitions.meaning: a jumble or miscellaneous collection of things
whimsically, a bag for carrying a rag, slang for a newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what odds and ends a newspaper delivery boy keeps in his shoulder bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscellaneous jumble of items is a mixed collection, and the second reading splits it into newspaper slang plus a carrier.

clue.text: Uneasy about one's being defiant

indicators.note: about means the word for uneasy goes round the rest

parts.note: restive means fidgety and uneasy
one is I, and 's is is, giving I + S

explanation.surface: Someone is uneasy about being openly defiant.
explanation.definitionFit: Being resistant to authority or opposing something is a form of defiance.

clue.text: Follower of good wicked rogue ensnared

indicators.note: ensnared means the shuffled rogue traps the word for good inside
wicked suggests the letters behave badly and are twisted out of order

parts.note: pi is short for pious, so good

explanation.surface: A good person is drawn in and trapped by a wicked rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good' looks like an adjective in the surface, but it is short for pious, trapped inside the jumbled rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: An avid fan who trails a band or celebrity is a devoted follower.

clue.text: Side area tracks run over

indicators.note: over means the tracks and run are turned upside down, read upward in a down clue

parts.note: lanes are tracks or narrow roads
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A sidetrack area is run over by trains.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club, so a side. 'over' turns LANES and R round to RSENAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A football team is a side, and this is one of London's best-known clubs.

clue.text: But sensor's broken, lacking this?

indicators.note: broken means the letters of but sensor's are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: An engineer remarks that a sensor which has broken evidently lacked sturdiness.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a sensor that breaks is one lacking the quality the anagram spells.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturdiness is exactly what a device that breaks easily lacks, so the clue points at it as the missing quality.

clue.text: Force us to drive away

indicators.note: to force something is to wrench it out of shape, so the two little words are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is being compelled to leave, as if pushed out of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' looks like part of the definition, but it signals rearranging US TO.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive someone away is to eject or expel them from a place or position.

clue.text: It pours, as Stephen saw

definitions.meaning: a phrase for heavy rain suddenly starting
St Stephen, before his martyrdom in Acts 7, said he saw the sky opened and the glory of God

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a common idiom for a sudden downpour and literally echoes the biblical vision of Stephen.

clue.text: More juicy duck man eats

indicators.note: eats means the word for a man swallows the duck, taking it inside

parts.note: Mister is the title for a man
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A man eating duck finds it juicier than expected.
explanation.definitionFit: Juicy means moist or succulent, so the comparative form means wetter.

clue.text: In detail, discuss right lost by one leaving our shores

indicators.note: lost by means the letter for right is shed by the emigrant word

parts.note: an expatriate is someone who has left their home country

explanation.surface: An emigrant debates fully what rights they forfeit by leaving the country.
explanation.definitionFit: To expatiate is to speak or write at great length, discussing something in full.

clue.text: Glower and run off, after getting sack

indicators.note: after getting places the word for running off behind the word for sacking

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them
to run off is to fly, flee

explanation.surface: A worker scowls and storms out after being dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glower' reads as scowl, but here it means something that glows: an insect lighting up at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A glowing beetle is literally a thing that glows, the crossword-only sense of glower as one who gives off light.

clue.text: An eccentric in Dundee?

definitions.meaning: a nutty, crazy person in informal speech
a Dundee cake is a rich Scottish cake full of dried fruit, so an example

explanation.definitionFit: Informally a nutty person is a crazy eccentric, and a Dundee cake is one kind of rich fruit-filled cake.

clue.text: As Pompadour was in court, did some cleaning

parts.note: to be up before a judge is to be in court
swept the floor, past tense of sweep

explanation.surface: Madame de Pompadour appeared at court and then tidied up.
explanation.walkthrough: The pompadour is a hairstyle, brushed up high off the forehead, named after Louis XV's mistress.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompadour hairstyle has the hair brushed high and back from the face, which is how swept-up hair is described.

clue.text: Contracted from arthropod a grave disease

indicators.note: contracted from suggests a piece taken out of the longer words, as a disease is caught from a source

explanation.surface: A grave illness is caught from an arthropod.
explanation.walkthrough: Podagra is the old medical name for gout, especially in the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Gout in the foot is a disease of the joints, and this is its classical medical name.

clue.text: Angry, being put into liquidation

definitions.meaning: a company is closed down and its assets sold

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means tense and agitated, and also describes a company formally closed down.

clue.text: Don't show up an FBI man, back of last month

indicators.note: back means the run an FBI man is read in reverse

parts.note: a fed is slang for a US federal agent
ult, short for ultimo, is old business letter shorthand for last month

explanation.surface: An FBI agent fails to turn up, as he has been since late last month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns round the whole of 'an FBI man', the article included; 'last month' is old business-letter shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: To fail to appear, as at a court hearing or match, is to forfeit by absence.

clue.text: Appreciate a medal given to a long-retired character

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking or appreciating it
MM is the Military Medal

explanation.surface: An old soldier is given a medal in retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: The character is a letter: an early Greek letter that dropped out of use long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic Greek letter fell out of the alphabet in antiquity, so it is a character retired long ago.

clue.text: Swung wildly and did not manage to hold line

indicators.note: to hold means the word for did not manage takes the line letter inside

parts.note: failed, did not succeed

explanation.surface: Someone thrashed about wildly and could not keep hold of a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: To flail is to wave or thrash about wildly, so this is its past tense.

clue.text: Beat up, taking on the river's current

indicators.note: taking on means the reversed beating word attaches the other pieces in front

parts.note: R is an abbreviation for river

indicators.note: up means the word for beat is read upward, backwards in a down clue

parts.note: to lam is to beat or thrash

explanation.surface: Someone beats upstream against the river's current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat up' reads as one phrase meaning assault, but 'up' is the reversal signal in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising column of warm air is an air current, the kind gliders and birds ride.

clue.text: Despair here, unsure of move in game

parts.note: being unsure is doubting
castling is a move in chess, as a verb to castle

explanation.surface: A chess player despairs, unsure which move to make.
explanation.walkthrough: In Bunyan's The Pilgrim's Progress, Giant Despair holds the pilgrims captive in his stronghold of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Giant Despair lives in this fortress in Bunyan's allegory, so it is literally the place where Despair is found.

clue.text: Oath once, say, taken by a duke

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: A duke swore an old-fashioned oath.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a mild archaic exclamation, an old minced oath in place of swearing by God.

clue.text: Not an arable parable?

parts.note: a fable set on a livestock holding rather than one growing crops, Orwell's political allegory

explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's novel is an allegorical tale set on a holding of livestock, not crops, hence a non-arable parable.

clue.text: Test piece to take place in identical surroundings

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for place sits inside the word for identical, which forms its surroundings

parts.note: identical means the same
Pl is the abbreviation for place in addresses

explanation.surface: An exam is to be held in an unchanged setting for fairness.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen taken for testing is a small portion representative of the whole.

clue.text: Tough sent to prison, say, for serious flogging

parts.note: tough means hard

indicators.note: say signals the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: a cell is a room in a prison

explanation.surface: A tough guy is jailed and given a severe beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flogging' suggests whipping, but means selling, as in an aggressive pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Flogging is British slang for selling, so a serious, pushy sales pitch is high-pressure selling.
